agent_vs_you: The agent built one 16:9 master and centre-cropped it to 9:16, betting on its still prompt ('musicians grouped in the central third'). A 9:16 crop of 16:9 keeps only 32% of the width; the model spread four or five musicians across the whole frame and the push-in widened them further, so the vertical version cuts the right-hand guitarist through the face at ~1-4 s. The user asked for both versions to 'fill the frame', which rules out padding, so the only safe route for a group of people is a native composition per aspect: recompose the wide still as a vertical one (an image-edit keeps the same musicians and look) and animate each. That costs a second clip, the price of not cutting faces. The text and audio parts of the agent's plan were fine. The judge's other fault ('speech' in the portrait audio) is a transcription artefact: the 16:9 version carries the same music track and was not flagged.

fix: 1) Planner rule / CHOOSING line: 'Several aspect versions of footage with people (a band, a group, two speakers): make each aspect natively (image, then an image-edit recomposing it into the other aspect, then image-to-video for each); never centre-crop 16:9 to 9:16, which keeps a third of the width. Crop only when there is one centred subject.' 2) Catalogue crop POORLY: 'groups spread across a wide frame: a 9:16 crop of 16:9 cuts the people at the sides'. 3) After any crop of footage with people, run frame + check 'is any face cut by the frame edge?'. 4) Grader: the transcription guard (the same track was 'speech' in one version and clean in the other).
